narrative.overview:
A calm stone-and-pine foundation where Arabic and Latin typography carry equal weight. The site doesn't decorate itself: tokens, mirrored layouts and component states are the graphics, because the system is the work being shown. Depth comes from panels sunk into the page, never from shadows. One pine accent marks the few things that matter on a page and nothing else.

The density is that of a well-made product spec: generous reading measure, quiet chrome, and precise small-scale detail in metadata and numbers. Both scripts are designed natively. Arabic has its own typefaces, line-height and zero tracking, not Latin settings mirrored.
keyCharacteristics: Warm stone neutrals with a single pine (light) / celadon (dark) accent.
Two type families per script: Space Grotesk + Figtree for Latin, Alexandria + Almarai for Arabic. JetBrains Mono only for numbers, code and Latin labels.
Depth from sunk panels and tonal steps, never shadows.
Soft-cornered controls and cards; pills only for chips.
Graphics come from the design system itself, never from illustration.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is one accent colour, and it appears at most three times per page.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Text uses `fg` or `muted` and nothing else. There is no third "subtle" level.

rules.name: The Two Lines Rule
rules.body: `line` is decoration and `line-strong` is affordance. Anything a user can interact with gets `line-strong`.

rules.name: The Semantic Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Semantic colours never appear in site chrome. They live only inside product screens and form messages.

rules.name: The Recompute Rule
rules.body: Any colour change must recompute the full contrast table, light and dark, before it ships.

rules.name: The Script Scale Rule
rules.body: Every size token carries a Latin and an Arabic value, resolved by the page language (`html[lang]`); never share one value across scripts. It has two parts. *Above Body* (hero, display, h1–h3), Arabic is set 10–15% smaller than Latin, because Arabic has no uppercase and Alexandria and Almarai have a larger effective body, so the same pixel size reads bigger. *From Body down*, proportion gives way to an absolute floor: Arabic body is never below 15px and Arabic micro never below 12px, because Arabic dots and diacritics carry meaning and blur first. Legibility wins over proportion. Never shrink below these values to make copy fit; cut the copy instead.

rules.name: The One Hero Rule
rules.body: `--size-hero` appears once per page, on the hero H1. Never hardcode a size above Display; add a named token instead.

rules.name: The Zero Tracking Rule
rules.body: Arabic letter-spacing is always 0. Negative tracking breaks the letter joins.

rules.name: The No Mono Arabic Rule
rules.body: Never set Arabic in JetBrains Mono. It has no Arabic glyphs, and the bidi algorithm scrambles the word order. Arabic labels use Almarai.

rules.name: The Equal Scripts Rule
rules.body: Arabic gets its own families, line-height and tracking. It is never Latin styling mirrored.

rules.name: The Sunk, Never Lifted Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows under cards or anything else. If something needs depth, sink it.

dos: Do keep the accent to three appearances or fewer per page.
Do use `line-strong` on every interactive edge and `line` only for decorative dividers.
Do give depth by sinking content into a `sunk` panel.
Do set Arabic in Alexandria (headings) and Almarai (body, labels, metadata), at 185% line-height and 0 tracking.
Do recompute the full light/dark contrast table after any colour change.
Do keep English and Arabic pages structurally identical.
donts: Don't look like a template portfolio: no hero gradients, glassmorphism, or mockups floating on blobs.
Don't over-animate: no scroll-jacking, parallax, or motion that slows a skimming reader.
Don't put soft grey drop shadows under cards.
Don't set Arabic text in a monospace font.
Don't apply negative letter-spacing to Arabic.
Don't chain metadata with middle dots ("Lead designer · Web + mobile · 2026"). Bilingual name pairs such as "دايرتنا · Da'eratna" are names, not metadata, and keep their dot.
Don't use decorative illustration. Graphics must come from the design system itself.
Don't use semantic colours in site chrome.
Don't add a third text colour, a second accent, or soft semantic backgrounds.
Don't use Inter or IBM Plex Sans Arabic. Both have been removed from the system.
